items.title: Average Br2 mass
items.description: Reports the average mass of a Br2 molecule as approximately 159.8 u, computed as a weighted sum of the three peaks at 157.836, 159.834, and 161.832 using their relative sizes of 0.2569, 0.4999, and 0.2431 (accepting 159.790–159.806 u).

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts diverged on whether to normalize by the 0.9999 sum of relative sizes; both 159.790 u and 159.806 u are defensible.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports 159.834 u (simple mean) or a value outside 159.790–159.806 u, indicating use of an unweighted average or another error.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly requested quantity; caught 1/2 flawed responses, moderate discrimination.

validation.gold_why: Reference reports no average Br2 mass.

items.title: Average atomic mass
items.description: Reports the average atomic mass of a bromine atom as approximately 79.9 u, obtained by dividing the average Br2 mass by two (accepting 79.895–79.903 u).

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts derived this from their respective Br2 averages; values diverged between 79.895 u and 79.903 u depending on normalization.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports ~159.8 u as the atomic mass (forgetting to halve) or a value outside 79.895–79.903 u.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly requested quantity; caught 1/2 flawed responses, moderate discrimination.

validation.gold_why: Reference reports no average atomic mass.

items.title: Light isotope abundance
items.description: Reports the percent abundance of the lighter bromine isotope as approximately 50.69% (accepting 50.6–50.7%).

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (e) requires percent abundance of the two isotopes; consensus value is 50.69%.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports 25.69% (using the raw 0.2569 peak size) or any other incorrect abundance.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core requested result; caught 1/2 negatives; gold=FAIL so capped below 5.

validation.gold_why: Reference reports no percent abundances.

items.title: Heavy isotope abundance

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (e) requires percent abundance of the two isotopes; consensus value is 49.31%.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports 24.31% (using the raw 0.2431 peak size) or any other incorrect abundance.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core requested result; caught 1/2 negatives; gold=FAIL so capped below 5.

validation.gold_why: Reference reports no percent abundances.

items.title: Avoids pq for middle peak

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Middle peak as pq not 2pq': using 0.4999 = pq alongside p² = 0.2569 yields inconsistent or impossible abundances.
provenance.discriminates: A response that sets up equations using pq = 0.4999 instead of 2pq = 0.4999, leading to inconsistent abundances.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific observed trap; caught 1/2 negatives; avoidance item weighted low.

validation.gold_why: Reference derives no abundances from peaks.

items.title: Framework and temperature
items.description: States that equilibrium statistical mechanics applies to strongly-correlated systems because the framework's central concept is a well-defined temperature, which depends on thermalization rather than on weak interactions.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts agree and the reference supports that equilibrium validity does not depend on interaction strength.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims strong correlations automatically place a system outside equilibrium statistical mechanics.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core answer fact; caught 2/2 negatives; item 3 gold=pass confirms satisfiability.

validation.gold_why: Reference does not state framework independence from interaction strength.

items.title: Framework ≠ perturbation theory
items.description: Avoids concluding that equilibrium statistical mechanics is inapplicable to strongly-correlated systems merely because perturbation theory or mean-field approximations fail.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Confusing perturbation with framework' (severity: high) identifies this conflation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that equates failure of weak-coupling approximations with failure of the equilibrium framework itself.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives but structural advantage in test design; discounted accordingly.

validation.gold_why: No mention of perturbation theory or mean-field failures.

items.title: Thermalization causality
items.description: Avoids asserting that strong interactions prevent thermalization, when the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis suggests strong interactions and chaos typically facilitate thermalization.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Reversing interaction-thermalization causality' (severity: medium) identifies this mistake.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims strong correlations cause non-thermal behavior by disrupting ergodicity.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; specific named mechanism, but pitfall advantage discounted.

validation.gold_why: Reference does not assert strong interactions prevent thermalization.

items.title: Framework independent of interaction strength
items.description: States that equilibrium statistical mechanics applies to strongly-correlated systems because the framework does not require weak interactions.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts agree and the reference supports that equilibrium validity does not depend on interaction strength.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims strong correlations automatically place a system outside equilibrium statistical mechanics.

validation.gold_why: Reference does not state framework independence from interaction strength.

items.title: Conditions for well-defined temperature
items.description: States that a well-defined temperature and partition function depend on thermalization, not on interaction strength per se, for strongly-correlated systems.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus claim across all rollouts; also matches the implicit constraint about temperature and partition function depending on thermalization.
provenance.discriminates: A response that ties the existence of temperature to weak coupling.

validation.gold_why: No statement linking temperature to thermalization rather than interaction strength.

items.title: Temperature as central concept
items.description: Identifies the existence of a well-defined temperature as the central concept determining whether equilibrium statistical mechanics applies to a system.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference highlights 'the concept of temperature' as the focal point, which the rollouts treated as merely one assumption among several.
provenance.discriminates: A response that lists many assumptions without identifying temperature as the load-bearing organizing idea.

validation.gold_why: Reference focuses on concept of temperature and conditions for SM applicability.

items.title: Tensor product observable
items.description: States that the simultaneous measurement observable is the tensor product of the local observable at photon A and the local observable at photon B.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts jumped to Born-rule probabilities without identifying that the joint measurement observable is O_A ⊗ O_B; the reference answer states only this fact.
provenance.discriminates: A response that computes joint probabilities but never names the composite observable as the tensor product of local observables.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core answer; caught 3/3 negatives, discrimination 1.00, gold=pass.

validation.gold_why: Reference explicitly states tensor product of local observables at A and B.

items.title: Commutator vanishes
items.description: States that the local observables on the two distinct subsystems commute exactly, i.e., [O_A⊗I, I⊗O_B]=0, so the tensor product measurement is well-defined.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts noted order-independence; the formal commutator [Π_A⊗I, I⊗Π_B]=0 was the consensus algebraic reason.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims order does not matter but never invokes the commutator that guarantees it.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explains why simultaneous measurement works; caught 2/3 negatives, gold=FAIL but genuinely necessary.

validation.gold_why: Commutator equation not mentioned in reference.

items.title: Joint probability formula
items.description: Gives the joint measurement probability P(+,-)=½sin²(α−β) for an anti-correlated outcome on the two photons.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts agreed on P(+,-)=1/2 sin²(α−β).
provenance.discriminates: A response that swaps sin² and cos² or omits the cross-term probability.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Concrete quantitative depth beyond the reference answer; caught 2/3 negatives.

validation.gold_why: Joint probability formula not given in reference.

items.title: Reduced density matrix

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollout 1 explicitly stated ρ_B = I/2 while rollouts 2 and 3 gave only the marginal probability P_B = 1/2; both are correct but the density matrix is more formal.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives only the marginal probability without the density matrix formalism.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Real added depth; caught 2/3 negatives, gold=FAIL, low importance to core answer.

validation.gold_why: Reduced density matrix not stated in reference.

items.title: No superluminal causation
items.description: Avoids endorsing the question's premise that measuring photon A 'instantly affects' photon B as a literal superluminal causal influence transmitted through space.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Causal direction asserted' warns against taking 'measuring A instantly affects B' literally as physical causation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states nonlocal correlation is acausal but elsewhere endorses the 'instantly affects' language as real causation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Guards the central interpretive trap; caught 0/3 but the misconception is question-embedded.

validation.gold_why: Reference does not endorse superluminal causal influence.

items.title: Reduced density matrix of B
items.description: Explicitly states the reduced density matrix of photon B as ρ_B = I/2.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollout 1 explicitly stated ρ_B = I/2 while rollouts 2 and 3 gave only the marginal probability P_B = 1/2; both are correct but the density matrix is more formal.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives only the marginal probability without the density matrix formalism.

validation.gold_why: Reduced density matrix not stated in reference.

items.title: IP final value
items.description: The response reports the ionization potential IP of X as 11.835 eV (or 11.84 eV).

provenance.evidence_detail: Required deliverable for sub-question a; reference gives a = 11.835 eV.
provenance.discriminates: A response giving IP = 1.18 eV or 15.19 eV or any other wrong value.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives, discrimination=1.00; final requested quantity.

validation.gold_why: Reports a = IP = 11.835 eV.

items.title: EA final value
items.description: The response reports the electron affinity EA of X as 3.358 eV (or 3.36 eV).

provenance.evidence_detail: Required deliverable for sub-question b; reference gives b = 3.358 eV.
provenance.discriminates: A response giving EA = 0.336 eV or 6.71 eV or any other wrong value.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives, discrimination=1.00; final requested quantity.

validation.gold_why: Reports b = EA = 3.358 eV.

items.title: Step 1 energy balance
items.description: The response writes the step 1 energy balance for the transfer of one electron between the two halves of X atoms as (N/2)×(IP − EA) = 409 kJ, with EA subtracted because electron attachment releases energy.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference and correct rollouts use IP − EA for step 1; pitfall EA-sign-in-step-1 addresses the wrong move of adding EA.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes (N/2)×(IP + EA) = 409 kJ or signs EA incorrectly.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core equation for first sub-question; load-bearing for entire derivation.

validation.gold_why: Writes (N/2)(a−b) = 409 kJ step; EA subtracted.

items.title: Step 2 energy balance
items.description: The response writes the step 2 energy balance for converting X⁻ ions to X⁺ as (N/2)×(IP + EA) = 733 kJ, because removing the extra electron costs +EA and ionizing the neutral costs +IP.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference uses a + b for step 2; pitfall Step-2-electron-count and EA-sign-in-step-2 address the wrong moves.
provenance.discriminates: A response that models X⁻ → X⁺ as one-electron removal costing only IP, giving (N/2)×IP = 733 kJ.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; core equation for second sub-question.

validation.gold_why: Writes (N/2)(a+b) = 733 kJ step; EA added.

items.title: Two-electron step 2
items.description: The response states that converting each X⁻ ion to X⁺ requires removing two electrons, one reversing the electron affinity and one ionizing the neutral X atom.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Step 2 electron count', severity high.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats X⁻ → X⁺ as a single-electron transition costing only IP.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; key physical reasoning distinguishing step 2 from step 1.

validation.gold_why: States X⁻ loses two electrons: +EA then +IP.

items.title: Uses N/2 not N
items.description: The response uses N/2 = 3.0115×10²³ as the number of electron-transfer pairs in each energy-balance equation, not the full Avogadro's number N = 6.023×10²³.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Using N instead of N/2', severity medium; reference uses N/2 throughout.
provenance.discriminates: A response that plugs full N into both equations, halving all per-atom eV values.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Critical setup; though caught 0/2, using full N would halve all values.

validation.gold_why: Uses N/2 in both energy-balance equations.

items.title: kJ to J conversion
items.description: The response converts the given energies to joules as 409×10³ J and 733×10³ J before dividing by N/2 and converting to eV.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'kJ to J omitted', severity medium.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses 409 and 733 directly in J, making final values too small by 1000×.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Necessary unit step; catching 0/2 but omission collapses all numeric results.

validation.gold_why: Uses 409×10³ and 733×10³ (J conversion).

items.title: eV conversion factor
items.description: The response uses the conversion 1 eV = 1.602×10⁻¹⁹ J to convert per-atom joule energies into eV.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference explicitly divides by 1.602×10⁻¹⁹ to obtain eV.
provenance.discriminates: A response that omits this conversion or uses an incorrect factor.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required to produce answers in eV; reference answer uses this factor.

validation.gold_why: Divides by 1.602×10⁻¹⁹ to convert to eV.

items.title: IP minus EA equals 8.477
items.description: The response obtains the intermediate value IP − EA = 8.477 eV from the 409 kJ step.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference gives a − b = 8.477; rollout 3 wrongly obtained 0.8476 due to an exponent error.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports IP − EA = 0.8476 eV or any value other than ~8.48 eV.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; intermediate result directly leading to final values.

validation.gold_why: Obtains a−b = 8.477 eV.

items.title: IP plus EA equals 15.194
items.description: The response obtains the intermediate value IP + EA = 15.194 eV from the 733 kJ step.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference gives a + b = 15.194; rollout 3 wrongly obtained 1.5194.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports IP + EA = 1.5194 eV or any value other than ~15.19 eV.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives, discrimination=1.00; key intermediate for both final answers.

validation.gold_why: Obtains a+b = 15.194 eV.

items.title: Avoids exponent slip
items.description: Avoids writing the per-atom energy for the 409 kJ step as ~1.358×10⁻¹⁹ J; the correct per-atom value is ~1.358×10⁻¹⁸ J.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Exponent in J/eV conversion', severity medium, observed in rollout 3.
provenance.discriminates: A response containing the off-by-10 exponent error that propagates to all final values.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; specific arithmetic trap observed in flawed responses.

validation.gold_why: No per-atom value written incorrectly; correct method used.

items.title: Both quantities reported
items.description: The response reports both IP and EA values in eV, explicitly labelled, rather than stopping after solving only one of the two.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Only one quantity reported', severity low; answer format demands two labelled values.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives only IP or only EA.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Question requests both quantities; ensures complete answer.

validation.gold_why: Reports both a (IP) and b (EA) in eV.

items.title: Simultaneous equations solved
items.description: The response solves the two simultaneous equations IP − EA = 8.477 and IP + EA = 15.194 to obtain IP and EA, e.g. by adding and subtracting the two equations.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference explicitly solves the system to reach a = 11.835 and b = 3.358.
provenance.discriminates: A response that fails to combine the two balances into solved IP and EA values.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives, discrimination=1.00; the step that produces both final answers.

validation.gold_why: Solves simultaneous equations for a and b.

items.title: Flow determined by K'(K)
items.description: The response states that the flow of the coupling constant is determined by the relation K'(K), obtained by iterating the renormalization group recursion.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference answer states: 'The correct flow of the coupling constant is determined by the relation K'(K).'
provenance.discriminates: A response that discusses flow qualitatively without stating that the K'(K) relation is the determining object.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core of reference answer; despite 0/2 discrimination, correctness collapses without it.

validation.gold_why: Flow determined by K'(K) explicitly stated.

items.title: Semi-group nature of RG
items.description: The response describes the renormalization group as a semi-group, where the transformation renormalizes the system by decreasing the number of sites and has no inverse.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference answer: 'reflecting the semi-group nature of the RG'; no rollout used the term semi-group.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats the RG as a full group with an inverse, or omits the semi-group characterization.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0.50 discrimination; captures semi-group nature and site reduction from reference.

validation.gold_why: Semi-group nature and site decrease mentioned.

items.title: Avoid missing 1/2 factor
items.description: Avoids writing the decimation recursion relation as K' = ln cosh(2K) without the factor of 1/2 in the 1D Ising model.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Missing 1/2 factor': dropping the 1/2 yields spurious fixed points.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes K' = ln cosh(2K) instead of K' = (1/2) ln cosh(2K).
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0.50 discrimination; specific algebraic error in the derivation of coupling constants.

validation.gold_why: No incorrect formula without 1/2 factor written.

items.title: Avoid reversed flow direction
items.description: Avoids asserting that the renormalization group flow in the 1D Ising model goes toward strong coupling, whether by stating K' > K for finite positive K or by claiming K* = ∞ attracts while K* = 0 repels.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Flow direction reversed': correct is K' < K for all finite K>0.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the flow drives K to infinity for any initial K>0.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Source 20 caught 2/2 negatives; merged with source 18 (1/2) covering same error.

validation.gold_why: No assertion that K' > K made.

items.title: Avoid finite-T transition claim
items.description: Avoids concluding that the 1D Ising model has a phase transition at a finite critical temperature T_c > 0.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Finite-T phase transition claimed': correct is no finite-T transition.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports a finite-T phase transition based on a spurious fixed point.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0.50 discrimination; false phase transition claim is a key conceptual trap.

validation.gold_why: No finite-T transition claimed.

items.title: Avoid reversed flow direction
items.description: The response avoids asserting that K' > K for finite positive K in the 1D Ising model recursion relation, which would predict flow toward strong coupling.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Flow direction reversed': correct is K' < K for all finite K>0.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the flow drives K to infinity for any initial K>0.

validation.gold_why: No assertion that K' > K made.

items.title: Isothermal bulk modulus
items.description: The response states that for the isothermal process the bulk modulus is K = P, equal to the static pressure, and avoids using K = γP for this case.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Swapped bulk modulus' (severity high): mixing up which thermodynamic variable is held constant in ∂P/∂V.
provenance.discriminates: A response that interchanges the two limits' bulk moduli, yielding v_T = v_S and Z_T = Z_S with wrong assignments.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core result for part (i); caught 1/2 negatives, discriminates swapped-modulus error.

validation.gold_why: Uses correct bulk modulus for each case, no swap.

items.title: Adiabatic bulk modulus
items.description: The response states that for the adiabatic process the bulk modulus is K = γP, where γ is the ratio of specific heats, and avoids using K = P for this case.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Swapped bulk modulus' (severity high): mixing up which thermodynamic variable is held constant in ∂P/∂V.
provenance.discriminates: A response that interchanges the two limits' bulk moduli, yielding v_T = v_S and Z_T = Z_S with wrong assignments.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core result for part (ii); caught 1/2 negatives, discriminates swapped-modulus error.

validation.gold_why: Uses correct bulk modulus for each case, no swap.

items.title: Isothermal wave speed
items.description: The response gives the isothermal acoustic wave speed as v = (P/ρ)^{1/2}, equivalently (T/m)^{1/2}, where ρ is the volumic mass density.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Omitting γ factor' (severity high): dropping γ from the adiabatic results so they coincide with isothermal.
provenance.discriminates: A response whose adiabatic results are numerically identical to the isothermal results.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly requested quantity; caught 1/2 negatives including omitted-γ error.

validation.gold_why: Includes γ factor in adiabatic speed and impedance.

items.title: Isothermal wave impedance
items.description: The response gives the isothermal wave impedance as Z = (Pρ)^{1/2}, equivalently (mT)^{1/2}n where n is the particle density, and avoids omitting the γ factor only in the adiabatic counterpart.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Omitting γ factor' (severity high): dropping γ from the adiabatic results so they coincide with isothermal.
provenance.discriminates: A response whose adiabatic results are numerically identical to the isothermal results.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly requested quantity; caught 1/2 negatives, verifies impedance sub-question addressed.

validation.gold_why: Includes γ factor in adiabatic speed and impedance.

items.title: Adiabatic wave speed
items.description: The response gives the adiabatic acoustic wave speed as v = (γP/ρ)^{1/2}, equivalently (γT/m)^{1/2}, and avoids writing it without the γ factor.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Omitting γ factor' (severity high): dropping γ from the adiabatic results so they coincide with isothermal.
provenance.discriminates: A response whose adiabatic results are numerically identical to the isothermal results.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly requested quantity; caught 1/2 negatives including omitted-γ error.
provenance.merged_mirror_text: The response gives the adiabatic wave impedance as Z = (γPρ)^{1/2}, equivalently (γmT)^{1/2}n, and avoids writing it without the γ factor.

validation.gold_why: Includes γ factor in adiabatic speed and impedance.

items.title: General wave speed relation
items.description: The response uses the general acoustic relation v = (K/ρ)^{1/2} connecting the wave speed to the bulk modulus and volumic mass density.

provenance.evidence_detail: All attempts and the reference agree on this starting formula; it is the load-bearing intermediate for both limits.
provenance.discriminates: A response that jumps to final answers without relating them to K and ρ, making the derivation uncheckable.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing intermediate formula; discrimination 0/2 but genuinely necessary for correctness.

validation.gold_why: Uses v = (K/ρ)^{1/2} as general acoustic relation.

items.title: General impedance relation
items.description: The response uses the general acoustic impedance relation Z = (Kρ)^{1/2}, equivalently Z = ρv, connecting impedance to bulk modulus and density.

provenance.evidence_detail: All attempts and the reference agree on Z = (Kρ)^{1/2} = ρv; it is the load-bearing intermediate for both impedance results.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses an inverted impedance formula such as Z = v/ρ or Z = 1/(ρv).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing intermediate formula; discrimination 0/2 but genuinely necessary for correctness.

validation.gold_why: Uses Z = (Kρ)^{1/2} as general impedance relation.

items.title: Adiabatic index definition
items.description: The response defines γ = C_P/C_V = (C_V + 1)/C_V and states that γ > 1 for the ideal classical gas with temperature-independent specific heat.

provenance.evidence_detail: All attempts correctly identified γ = C_P/C_V > 1, and this is load-bearing for the adiabatic results and the comparison between limits.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses γ ≤ 1 or never defines γ, making the comparison between limits unjustified.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required for correctness of adiabatic results; discrimination 0/2 but no near-duplicate covers it.

validation.gold_why: Defines γ = C_P/C_V and states γ > 1.

items.title: Adiabatic exceeds isothermal
items.description: The response states that the adiabatic wave velocity and impedance are larger than the isothermal values by a factor of γ^{1/2} (i.e., v_S/v_T = γ^{1/2} and Z_S/Z_T = γ^{1/2}), because γ > 1.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus among attempts and reference that v_S/v_T = Z_S/Z_T = sqrt(γ) > 1; the reference explicitly says adiabatic values are always larger.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the two limits give equal results or that isothermal values are larger.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; highest discrimination item, captures the key comparison.

validation.gold_why: States adiabatic v and Z are larger than isothermal by γ>1.

items.title: Frequency-regime identification
items.description: The response identifies the adiabatic limit as achieved at higher wave frequencies because the oscillation period is too short for heat exchange, and the isothermal limit as the low-frequency regime where the period is long enough for temperature to equilibrate.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Frequency–regime reversal' (severity high): inverting which limit corresponds to high vs low frequency.
provenance.discriminates: A response that swaps the frequency assignments, saying fast oscillations allow temperature equilibration.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly answers final sub-question; caught 1/2 negatives, absorbs frequency-reversal pitfall.

validation.gold_why: Correctly assigns adiabatic to high frequency, isothermal to low.

items.title: Isothermal equation of state
items.description: The response uses the ideal-gas equation of state P = NT/V (or equivalently P = nT) under isothermal conditions to derive the isothermal bulk modulus K = P.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly states P = NT/V at X = T = const and differentiates to get K = P; this is the load-bearing step for the isothermal case.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states K = P without connecting it to the ideal-gas equation of state under constant temperature.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing derivation step; caught 1/2 negatives, anchors K = P in first principles.

items.title: Theta difference form
items.description: The final expression for n(E) contains the Heaviside theta function factor θ(E−E_b)−θ(E−E_t) or an equivalent form such as θ(2|J|−|E−E_s|).

items.title: Substitution x = ka
items.description: The derivation uses the substitution x = ka with dk = dx/a, by which the integral limits are transformed from [−π/a, π/a] to [−π, π].

provenance.calibration_rationale: Foundational step for cancelling a; no measured discrimination but enables correct prefactor.

items.title: Root equation
items.description: The derivation identifies the roots of the delta function argument by solving cos(ka) = (E_s − E)/(2J).

items.title: Two symmetric roots
items.description: The derivation accounts for both symmetric roots ±k₀ of the delta function argument within [−π/a, π/a], each contributing a factor 1/|g'(k_i)| to the integral.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Counting only one root' (severity high): forgetting the second root at −k₀ halves the result.
provenance.discriminates: A response that identifies only k₀ = arccos[−(E−E_s)/(2J)] and misses −k₀, yielding N/(π√(4J²−(E−E_s)²)) instead of 2N/(π√(4J²−(E−E_s)²)).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; two-root counting is a key intermediate with real discriminative power.

validation.gold_why: Expression accounts for both roots symmetrically

items.title: Delta identity
items.description: The derivation applies the identity δ(g(k)) = Σ_i δ(k−k_i)/|g'(k_i)|, by which the integral of the delta function is transformed into a sum over roots.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Core transformation identity; explains how the delta integral becomes a discrete sum.

items.title: Jacobian derivative
items.description: The derivation computes the Jacobian |g'(k)| = 2Ja|sin(ka)| from the derivative of the 2J cos(ka) term in the delta function argument.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific intermediate derivative; enables the correct Jacobian factor in the final expression.

items.title: sin² substitution
items.description: The derivation substitutes sin²(k₀a) = 1 − ((E−E_s)/(2J))² to express the Jacobian factor in terms of E, E_s, and J.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Key algebraic step linking k-space to E-space; grounds the sqrt denominator.

items.title: Band edges
items.description: The derivation identifies the band edges E_b = E_s − 2|J| and E_t = E_s + 2|J|, where cos(ka) = ±1 and the sqrt(4J²−(E−E_s)²) denominator vanishes.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific band-edge values; define the theta function arguments in the final expression.

items.title: Support to theta
items.description: The derivation explains that the Heaviside theta function arises because the roots of the delta function argument exist only when |E−E_s| ≤ 2|J|, so the integral evaluates to zero outside this range.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly answers the 'explain' part; theta arises from root existence condition.

items.title: Factor of 2 from roots

provenance.calibration_rationale: Intermediate factor from combining two roots; contributes to the correct prefactor.

items.title: Avoids spurious factor of a

items.title: Avoids wrong ordering

provenance.calibration_rationale: Zero discrimination; wrong ordering gives negative DOS, a sign-error trap.

validation.gold_why: Uses standard θ(E−E_b)−θ(E−E_t) form

items.title: Complete final expression

provenance.calibration_rationale: Synthesis criterion; verifies the final expression assembles prefactor and support factor correctly.

validation.gold_why: N/π present in prefactor after a cancels

items.title: Common fungal infection
items.description: The response describes tinea corporis as a common fungal infection.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference frames tinea corporis as a common fungal infection characterized by pruritic, enlarging rashes.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; minor framing detail that adds context but is not essential.

validation.gold_why: Describes tinea corporis as a common fungal infection.

items.title: Avoids tinea versicolor

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Tinea versicolor misdiagnosis' notes this error leads to recommending ketoconazole shampoo or selenium sulfide lotion.
provenance.discriminates: A response that diagnoses tinea versicolor and recommends ketoconazole 2% or selenium sulfide 2.5%.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; this specific misdiagnosis was a real observed trap with high discrimination.

validation.gold_why: Does not diagnose tinea versicolor.

items.title: Avoids oral/systemic therapy
items.description: Avoids recommending an oral or systemic treatment such as terbinafine or griseofulvin, keeping the treatment topical.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Oral instead of topical' warns against systemic therapy when the question asks for topical treatment.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names an oral agent such as terbinafine 250 mg PO daily.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 0/2; relevant route error but not observed in flawed responses, so minimal weight.

validation.gold_why: Does not recommend oral antifungal; keeps topical.

items.title: Avoids STI diagnosis
items.description: Avoids diagnosing a sexually transmitted infection based on the sexually active status and inconsistent condom use.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'STI over-interpretation' warns against anchoring on sexual activity to diagnose secondary syphilis or other STIs.
provenance.discriminates: A response that recommends an STI workup or systemic antibiotics such as IM penicillin instead of a topical antifungal.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 0/2; sexual history is a deliberate distractor but flawed responses did not take this bait.

validation.gold_why: Does not diagnose an STI from sexual history.

items.title: Rash location on chest
items.description: The response places the rash on the chest as described in the clinical vignette.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question structure identifies rash_location as chest, which must be reflected in the diagnostic reasoning.
provenance.discriminates: A response that places the rash on the groin or another body site.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 0/2; anchoring location supports correct diagnosis and avoids anatomical mislabeling.

validation.gold_why: Mentions rash on the chest.

items.title: Lifeguard as fungal support
items.description: The response states that the lifeguard occupation supports the diagnosis of a fungal infection due to water exposure.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts treated the lifeguard occupation as a distractor; the reference uses it as supporting evidence for dermatophyte infection.
provenance.discriminates: A response that dismisses the lifeguard occupation as a red herring rather than using it to support fungal diagnosis.

validation.gold_why: States lifeguard water exposure supports fungal diagnosis.

items.title: Minimum thickness value
items.description: States the minimum coating thickness as t = 0.10 μm (or approximately 1042 Å) for part (a).

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (a) asks for the minimum thickness; the reference gives t = λ/(4n₁) = 0.10 μm.
provenance.discriminates: A response that computes 2083 Å or 868 Å instead of 1042 Å.

validation.gold_why: States t = λ/(4n₁) = 0.10 μm.

items.title: Destructive interference condition
items.description: Uses the destructive interference condition 2n₁t = λ/2 with n₁ = 1.2 and λ = 5000 Å for the coating film.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference writes 2n₁t = λ/2 as the condition for antiphase reflected beams.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses 2n₁t = mλ (one net π shift) or 2n₁t = λ (wrong condition).

validation.gold_why: Uses 2n₁t = λ/2 explicitly.

items.title: Unequal coefficients explanation
items.description: Part (b) explains that the reflected intensity is nonzero because the reflection coefficients at the two surfaces of the coating are unequal (R₁ ≠ R₂).

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (b) asks why reflection is small but not zero; the reference shows R₁ ≠ R₂.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims destructive interference alone should give zero, or that does not identify unequal amplitudes.

validation.gold_why: Explains R₁ ≠ R₂ causes nonzero reflected intensity.

items.title: Ideal coating index value
items.description: States the ideal coating index for zero reflection as n' = √(1 × 1.4) ≈ 1.18.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (b) requires the changed index value; the reference gives n' = √(n₀n₂) = 1.18.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives 1.2 (arithmetic mean), 1.3, or no ideal index.

validation.gold_why: States n' = √(n₀n₂) = 1.18.

items.title: Reflection coefficient formula
items.description: Gives a reflection coefficient formula — either R = [(nA − nB)/(nA + nB)]² or r = (nA − nB)/(nA + nB) — for the surfaces of the coating.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference uses R = [(nA − nB)/(nA + nB)]²; rollouts used the amplitude version r, both physically valid.
provenance.discriminates: A response that explains unequal reflection qualitatively without providing the quantitative formula.

validation.gold_why: Gives R = [(nA−nB)/(nA+nB)]² formula.

items.title: Zero-reflection amplitude condition
items.description: States that zero reflected intensity requires the reflection coefficients at the two surfaces to be equal (R₁ = R₂).

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference sets R₁ = R₂ as the condition for zero resultant reflected light.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims thickness alone can produce zero reflection without addressing amplitude matching.

validation.gold_why: States R₁ = R₂ required for zero reflection.

items.title: Vacuum wavelength used
items.description: Uses λ = 5000 Å as the vacuum (air) wavelength in the optical path difference formula 2n₁t.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Forget vacuum wavelength' pitfall warns against double-dividing by n₁ using the in-medium wavelength.
provenance.discriminates: A response that substitutes λ/n₁ into the interference condition, obtaining d = λ/(4n₁²).

validation.gold_why: Uses λ = 5000 Å as vacuum wavelength in 2n₁t.

items.title: Specific coefficient values
items.description: Computes or states the reflection coefficients at the air–coating interface as R₁ = ((1.2 − 1.0)/(1.2 + 1.0))² and at the coating–glass interface as R₂ = ((1.2 − 1.4)/(1.2 + 1.4))².

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly computes R₁ and R₂ using n₀ = 1, n₁ = 1.2, n₂ = 1.4.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the coefficients are equal without computing them, or that computes them incorrectly.

validation.gold_why: Writes R₁ and R₂ with correct symbolic index values.

items.title: Geometric mean derivation
items.description: Derives n' = √(n₀n₂) from the condition R₁ = R₂ for the two surfaces of the coating.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference solves (n'−n₀)/(n'+n₀) = (n'−n₂)/(n'+n₂) to obtain n' = √(n₀n₂).
provenance.discriminates: A response that states n' = 1.18 without deriving it, or that derives it from the wrong condition.

validation.gold_why: Derives n' = √(n₀n₂) from R₁ = R₂ condition.

items.title: Change index not thickness
items.description: States that the coating refractive index must be changed (rather than the thickness) to make the reflected intensity zero.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (b) asks 'what needs to be changed'; the reference changes n₁ to n', not t.
provenance.discriminates: A response that suggests adjusting the thickness further or changing the wavelength to achieve zero reflection.

validation.gold_why: States index must change, not thickness.

items.title: Antiphase with unequal amplitudes
items.description: States that the two reflected beams are in antiphase (destructive interference) but have unequal amplitudes, so cancellation is incomplete.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference shows the beams interfere destructively (antiphase) but R₁ ≠ R₂ prevents full cancellation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the beams are not in antiphase, or that equal amplitudes are not required for cancellation.

validation.gold_why: States destructive interference but unequal intensities, incomplete cancellation.

items.title: Avoids one-phase-shift thickness
items.description: Avoids stating the minimum thickness as 5000/(2 × 1.2) ≈ 2083 Å, which would result from counting only one π phase shift at the coating surfaces.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'One phase shift counted' and 'Admits only one phase shift' pitfalls both produce d ≈ 2083 Å.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives 2083 Å as the minimum coating thickness.

validation.gold_why: Gives 0.10 μm, not 2083 Å.

items.title: Avoids arithmetic mean index
items.description: Avoids claiming the ideal coating index equals the arithmetic mean (1 + 1.4)/2 = 1.2, which would imply no change is needed.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Arithmetic mean for index' pitfall yields exactly 1.2, creating false confirmation that the given index is already ideal.
provenance.discriminates: A response that concludes the given n₁ = 1.2 already satisfies the zero-reflection condition.

validation.gold_why: States ideal index 1.18, not arithmetic mean 1.2.

items.title: Avoids wrong index direction
items.description: Avoids stating that the coating index must increase from 1.2 to achieve zero reflected intensity.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Wrong direction of change' pitfall claims Δn ≈ +0.017 or an increase to 1.217.
provenance.discriminates: A response that says the index must increase rather than decrease from 1.2.

validation.gold_why: Ideal index 1.18 is below 1.2, implies decrease.

items.title: Avoids double-dividing wavelength
items.description: Avoids computing the coating thickness as 5000/(4 × 1.2²) ≈ 868 Å by substituting the in-medium wavelength λ/n₁ into the interference condition.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Forget vacuum wavelength' pitfall double-divides by n₁, giving d = λ/(4n₁²) ≈ 868 Å.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses the in-medium wavelength and obtains a thickness near 868 Å.

validation.gold_why: Uses λ/(4n₁), not λ/(4n₁²).

items.title: Five components stated
items.description: The response states that the fine structure of the Rayleigh light scattering lines in amorphous solids consists of five components.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts described a three-component structure (central + one Brillouin doublet) rather than the correct five-component structure.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that describe the spectrum qualitatively without committing to the explicit count of five components.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; the total count is the load-bearing fact of the answer.

validation.gold_why: Explicitly states five components.

items.title: One undisplaced component
items.description: The response identifies one undisplaced component as part of the fine structure of the Rayleigh scattering lines.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer explicitly states 'one undisplaced component'; all rollouts mentioned a central peak but the reference frames it as part of a five-component count.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that omit the central elastic peak entirely or fail to label it as one of the five components.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core reference content; 0/3 discrimination because flawed responses still included it.

validation.gold_why: Identifies one undisplaced component.

items.title: Two displaced pairs
items.description: The response states that there are two pairs of displaced components in the fine structure of the Rayleigh light scattering lines.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer explicitly states 'two pairs of displaced components'; rollouts described only one pair definitively.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that mention only one displaced pair (longitudinal) and omit the second pair.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; the pair structure is a central discriminator.

validation.gold_why: States two pairs of displaced components.

items.title: Transverse acoustic pair
items.description: The response states that the other pair of displaced components is obtained from scattering by transverse acoustic waves.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts hedged on or omitted the transverse pair, treating it as optional or geometry-dependent, while the reference states it as a definite second pair.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that treat transverse acoustic scattering as conditional, weak, or geometry-dependent rather than as a definite component of the fine structure.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; the transverse pair is the key challenging fact.
provenance.merged_mirror_text: The response states that one pair of displaced components is obtained from scattering by longitudinal acoustic waves.

validation.gold_why: Other pair from transverse acoustic waves.

items.title: Qualitative description
items.description: The response describes the fine structure of the Rayleigh light scattering lines qualitatively, without relying on numerical calculations of frequency shifts or intensities.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question structure notes the implicit constraint that the answer must be qualitative, not numerical.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that attempt numerical calculations of Brillouin shifts instead of providing the requested qualitative description.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Question explicitly requests qualitative description; 0/3 discrimination, minor depth.

validation.gold_why: Describes qualitatively in prose.

items.title: Stokes and anti-Stokes
items.description: The response states that each pair of displaced components includes both a Stokes-shifted and an anti-Stokes-shifted component.

provenance.evidence_detail: The mined pitfall 'Anti-Stokes line dropped' warns against omitting the time-reversed anti-Stokes process.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that describe one displaced line per phonon branch instead of symmetric pairs.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Real physics depth beyond terse reference; 0/3 discrimination, low weight.

validation.gold_why: Mentions pairs, does not drop anti-Stokes.

items.title: Transverse pair definite
items.description: Avoids describing the transverse acoustic displaced pair as present only under certain sample geometries rather than as a definite component of the five-component structure in amorphous solids.

provenance.evidence_detail: The mined pitfall 'Transverse pair omitted' was observed in all rollouts, which hedged on transverse components.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that frame transverse Brillouin components as conditional or weak rather than intrinsic.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/3 negatives; discounted for structural pitfall advantage.

validation.gold_why: Treats transverse pair as definite component.

items.title: Avoids crystal selection rules
items.description: Avoids applying crystalline momentum-conservation selection rules that would forbid or strongly suppress transverse acoustic scattering in amorphous solids.

provenance.evidence_detail: The mined pitfall 'Crystal selection rules applied' warns against uncritically carrying over crystal selection rules to glasses.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that claim only longitudinal modes contribute based on crystalline backscattering selection rules.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/3 negatives; discounted for structural advantage, less central than count.

validation.gold_why: Does not apply crystal selection rules.

items.title: Longitudinal acoustic pair
items.description: The response states that one pair of displaced components is obtained from scattering by longitudinal acoustic waves.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts correctly identified a longitudinal acoustic Brillouin doublet.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that fail to attribute any displaced pair to longitudinal acoustic waves.

validation.gold_why: One pair from longitudinal acoustic waves.

items.title: Names transference
items.description: The response identifies the situation as transference in which the patient projects feelings onto the therapist, with the direction of feelings flowing from patient to therapist rather than from therapist to patient.

items.title: Combined mechanisms

items.title: Avoids immunologic overcall
items.description: Avoids invoking immunologic infertility or anti-sperm antibody positivity as the diagnosis given the stated absence of agglutination.

provenance.discriminates: Responses that add immunologic infertility or anti-sperm antibody as a contributing diagnosis despite negative agglutination.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 0/2 negatives; names specific overcall trap relevant to absent agglutination.

items.title: Diagnosis is mild oligospermia
items.description: States the most likely diagnosis is mild oligospermia.

items.title: Inertial frame trajectory
items.description: The response models the ball as traveling in a straight line at constant velocity in the inertial frame after leaving the surface, with no gravitational force acting on it.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts and the reference use the inertial-frame straight-line trajectory with no real gravity, consistent with the implicit constraint that the only gravity is apparent from rotation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that applies a uniform gravitational field g in the inertial frame and uses a parabolic trajectory, yielding the Earth range of 120 m.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core modeling assumption; caught 1/2 negatives, load-bearing for all downstream geometry.

validation.gold_why: States no forces act in inertial frame, straight-line motion.

items.title: Speed composition V ± v_t
items.description: The response composes the inertial tangential velocity as V + v_t for the prograde hit and V − v_t for the retrograde hit, where V = √(gR) is the habitat's tangential velocity and v_t is the batter's tangential component.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts add the tangential component to V for prograde and subtract for retrograde; the reference gives u_± = √(v_y² + (V ± v_x)²).
provenance.discriminates: A response that swaps the signs, assigning the larger inertial speed to the retrograde direction or vice versa.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key intermediate step; caught 1/2 negatives, distinguishes parallel vs antiparallel cases.

validation.gold_why: Uses u_+ with (V + v_x) and u_- with (V - v_x).

items.title: Prograde distance 108 m
items.description: The response reports the prograde (along rotation) distance along the surface as approximately 108 m.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts and the reference agree on L_+ ≈ 108 m for the forward hit.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports a prograde distance of 132 m due to a sign error, or never computes the prograde case.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required comparison value; caught 1/2 negatives, needed to identify maximum.

validation.gold_why: Reports L_+ ≈ 108 m.

items.title: Retrograde distance 132 m
items.description: The response reports the retrograde (against rotation) distance along the surface as approximately 132 m.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts 1 and 2 and the reference give L_- ≈ 132 m; rollout 3 gave 133.1 m due to an intermediate rounding error in arctan.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives 133.1 m from premature rounding, or gives only the prograde value of 108 m.
provenance.calibration_rationale: The final answer; caught 2/2 negatives, highest discrimination and directly answers the question.

validation.gold_why: Reports L_- ≈ 132 m.

items.title: Optimal direction opposite rotation
items.description: The response states that hitting in the direction opposite to the habitat's rotation gives the furthest distance.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts and the reference identify the retrograde direction as optimal, since L_- > L_+.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims hitting with the direction of rotation maximizes distance, or does not specify the optimal direction.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly answers the qualitative part of the question; caught 1/2 negatives, essential conclusion.

validation.gold_why: States hit opposite to habitat rotation for furthest distance.

items.title: Arc length along surface
items.description: The response computes the distance measured along the surface of the habitat as the arc length R|Δθ|, where Δθ is the angular separation, rather than the chord length 2R sin(Δθ/2).

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Arc length vs chord length' pitfall (low severity) notes the formulas are numerically close here but conceptually different.
provenance.discriminates: A response that explicitly uses the chord formula 2R sin(Δθ/2) as its distance measure, which would be wrong for larger angles.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Question explicitly asks for distance along surface; caught 1/2 negatives, absorbs chord-length pitfall.

validation.gold_why: Uses arc length 2Rβ, not chord length.

items.title: Surface rotation during flight
items.description: The response subtracts the angle ωt_f through which the habitat surface rotates during the ball's flight from the inertial-frame landing angle φ to obtain the surface angular separation Δθ = φ − ωt_f.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts compute the habitat rotation angle ωt ≈ 0.181 rad and subtract it from the inertial intersection angle φ ≈ 0.168 rad, yielding the small difference Δθ ≈ 0.0132 rad.
provenance.discriminates: A response that computes only the inertial intersection angle φ ≈ 0.168 rad and reports D ≈ Rφ ≈ 1675 m without accounting for surface rotation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key step converting inertial to rotating-frame arc; caught 1/2 negatives, without it answer is wrong.

validation.gold_why: Subtracts s_2 = θR rotation contribution from s_1.

items.title: Avoids only prograde answer
items.description: Avoids reporting only the prograde distance of 108 m as the maximum by also computing the retrograde case and selecting the larger value of 132 m.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Only prograde direction tried' pitfall (high severity) notes the temptation to assume hitting with rotation gives more range and stop at 108 m.
provenance.discriminates: A response that computes only the forward hit and reports 108 m as the furthest distance.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; strong discrimination against incomplete two-case analysis.

validation.gold_why: Computes both cases and selects 132 m.

items.title: Avoids radius in km units
items.description: Avoids using R = 10 (in km) directly in formulas involving g = 10 m/s², and instead converts to R = 10000 m before computing V = √(gR).

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Radius unit not converted' pitfall (high severity) shows that using R = 10 gives V = 10 m/s, making rotation negligible and yielding a flat-Earth-like answer.
provenance.discriminates: A response that plugs R = 10 into √(gR) without converting from kilometers to meters.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Unit-mismatch trap; caught 1/2 negatives, directly corrupts velocity magnitude.

validation.gold_why: Correct numerical results imply R in meters.

items.title: Avoids intermediate rounding
items.description: Avoids premature rounding of the inertial landing angle φ or the habitat rotation angle ωt_f before computing their small difference Δθ ≈ 0.0132 rad, which would yield 133.1 m instead of 132 m.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Intermediate rounding in arctan' pitfall (observed in rollout 3) shows that rounding φ to 0.16745 rad loses the critical digits in the cancellation, producing 133.1 m.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports 133.1 m due to rounding intermediates to fewer than the needed significant figures in the near-cancellation of φ and ωt.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; rounding a small difference of large angles is a high-impact error.

validation.gold_why: No premature rounding; gives 132 m.

items.title: Inertial speed expressions
items.description: The response provides the inertial speeds in the form u_± = √(g(R ± √(2LR) + L)) or equivalent symbolic expressions for both prograde and retrograde cases.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference supplies the closed-form u_± = √(g(R ± √(2LR) + L)), which the rollouts compute numerically rather than symbolically.
provenance.discriminates: A response that only gives numerical inertial speeds without the underlying symbolic structure relating them to R, L, and g.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; compact symbolic form validates the full speed composition.

validation.gold_why: Gives u_± = √(g(R ± √(2LR) + L)) explicitly.

items.title: Closed-form arc distance
items.description: The response gives the closed-form expression L_± = 2R|sin⁻¹(√(L/2)/√(R ± √(2LR) + L)) − √(RL/2)/(R ± √(2LR) + L)| or an equivalent compact symbolic formula for the surface distance.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference supplies this compact algebraic form, while the rollouts use arctan and numerical computation for equivalent results.
provenance.discriminates: A response that provides only numerical results without any symbolic arc-distance formula tying the answer to the physical parameters.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; adds depth but is not strictly necessary for the numerical answer.

validation.gold_why: Gives the full closed-form expression for L_±.

items.title: Retrograde distance value
items.description: The response reports the retrograde (against rotation) distance along the surface as approximately 132 m.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts 1 and 2 and the reference give L_- ≈ 132 m; rollout 3 gave 133.1 m due to an intermediate rounding error in arctan.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives 133.1 m from premature rounding, or gives only the prograde value of 108 m.

validation.gold_why: Reports L_- ≈ 132 m.

validation.gold_why: States closed aortic valve prevents blood flowing back into heart.

items.title: Aortic valve closed
items.description: States that the aortic valve remains closed at the end of ventricular diastole.

items.title: Coronary not compressed
items.description: States that coronary arteries are not compressed by the relaxed ventricles, allowing blood to supply the heart muscle.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus across rollouts: low intramyocardial pressure and minimized extravascular compression explain high coronary flow; reference states ventricles are 'not compressed by the contracting heart.'

items.title: Ventricles relaxed
items.description: States that the ventricles are fully relaxed at the end of ventricular diastole.

provenance.discriminates: A response that describes the ventricles as contracting or partially contracted at end-diastole.

items.title: Diastole-systole transition
items.description: States that as ventricular diastole concludes and transitions into systole, the aortic valve will soon open to initiate blood flow into the aorta.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Adds transition context; caught 1/2 negatives; gold pass.

items.title: Avoids coronary systolic peak
items.description: Avoids stating that coronary flow is low at the end of ventricular diastole because the heart is not contracting.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Coronary flow timing reversed' (high severity): the intuition that flow to an organ should be highest when it is working hardest leads to the incorrect claim that coronary flow is low at end-diastole.
provenance.discriminates: A response that correctly identifies the end-diastolic phase but reverses the coronary flow direction, claiming it is suppressed because the heart is relaxed.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Targets a specific misconception about coronary flow timing; caught 1/2 negatives; gold pass.

validation.gold_why: Avoids stating coronary flow is low at end of diastole.

items.title: Avoids early aortic flow
items.description: Avoids claiming that aortic flow begins or increases at the end of ventricular diastole, including by attributing it to atrial contraction.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfalls 'Aortic valve opened early' (high) and 'Atrial systole ejects to aorta' (high): end-diastole is adjacent to systole, and atrial contraction is easily conflated with ventricular ejection, leading to the false claim that aortic flow starts during late diastole.
provenance.discriminates: A response that blurs the diastole-systole boundary and claims atrial systole or ventricular preparation causes aortic flow before the aortic valve opens.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Targets a specific wrong claim about premature aortic flow; caught 1/2 negatives; gold pass.

validation.gold_why: Avoids claiming aortic flow begins at end of diastole.

items.title: Avoids runoff conflation
items.description: Avoids treating aortic flow across the aortic valve as the same as continued peripheral runoff within the aorta during diastole.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Aortic flow vs aortic runoff' (medium severity): the windkessel effect causes genuine forward movement of blood within the aorta during diastole, but flow across the aortic valve is zero; responses that report aortic flow as non-zero because of peripheral runoff are making a distinct conceptual error.
provenance.discriminates: A response that says aortic flow is moderate or non-zero because blood continues flowing through the aorta to the periphery, rather than distinguishing valve flow from intravascular runoff.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Real conceptual distinction; 0 discrimination in small sample but names a genuine error.

validation.gold_why: Does not conflate aortic valve flow with peripheral runoff.

items.title: Shared RT mechanism
items.description: States that all three types—retroviruses, retroviruslike elements, and retroposons—use reverse transcription to insert DNA copies of their RNA into new sites in the cell's genome.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) asks for similarities; the reference opens with this as the core shared mechanism.
provenance.discriminates: A response that lists differences but never states the shared reverse-transcription mechanism.

validation.gold_why: First sentence states all three use reverse transcription to insert DNA copies into genome.

items.title: All encode reverse transcriptase
items.description: States that each of the three types of retrotransposons encodes the enzyme reverse transcriptase.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts correctly identified this shared feature, and the reference confirms it.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims only retroviruses encode reverse transcriptase.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required shared feature; measured discrimination 0.33, essential to the answer.

validation.gold_why: Second sentence states reverse transcriptase is encoded by each type.

items.title: Cytoplasmic RT viruses/RLEs
items.description: States that reverse transcription of the RNA occurs in the cytoplasm for both retroviruses and retroviruslike elements.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts either omitted or ambiguously stated the compartment; the reference specifies cytoplasm for these two classes.
provenance.discriminates: A response that omits the subcellular site or says nucleus for retroviruses/RLEs.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Perfect discrimination 1.0; key distinguishing locus fact for two of three types.

validation.gold_why: States reverse transcription occurs in cytoplasm for retroviruses and RLEs.

items.title: Nuclear RT for retroposons
items.description: States that reverse transcription occurs in the nucleus for retroposons.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollout 2 ambiguously wrote 'nucleus/cytoplasm' for retroposons; rollouts 1 and 3 omitted it; the reference says nucleus.
provenance.discriminates: A response that says cytoplasm or is ambiguous about the retroposon reverse transcription site.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Perfect discrimination 1.0; key distinguishing locus fact for retroposons.

validation.gold_why: States reverse transcription occurs in nucleus for retroposons.

items.title: Assembly protein viruses/RLEs
items.description: States that retroviruses and retroviruslike elements encode a protein that functions in the assembly of virus or viruslike particles in the cytoplasm.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts mentioned VLPs and gag but did not frame the encoded protein's functional role in cytoplasmic particle assembly as the reference does.
provenance.discriminates: A response that says RLEs form VLPs but never identifies the encoded assembly protein or its cytoplasmic function.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Perfect discrimination 1.0; distinguishes viruses and RLEs from retroposons on protein function.

validation.gold_why: States retroviruses and RLEs encode protein for assembly of virus/viruslike particles in cytoplasm.

items.title: Nuclear-transport protein retroposons
items.description: States that retroposons encode a different protein that appears to bind to the retroposon RNA and convey it into the nucleus.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts described retroposon proteins as endonuclease/RT or RNA-binding (ORF1/ORF2) but never framed the function as nuclear transport of retroposon RNA.
provenance.discriminates: A response that describes ORF1/ORF2 functions for retroposons but never states the nuclear-transport role.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Perfect discrimination 1.0; specific functional contrast with the virus and RLE assembly protein.

validation.gold_why: States retroposons encode different protein binding RNA and conveying it to nucleus.

items.title: Retroviral RNA packaged for exit

items.title: env gene required for exit

items.title: Momentum expectation integral
items.description: Writes the momentum expectation value as ⟨p⟩ = −iℏ ∫_{−∞}^{+∞} dx ψ(x) ψ'(x).

items.title: Boundary term evaluates to zero
items.description: Evaluates the boundary term [ψ²(x)]_{−∞}^{+∞} = 0 so that the momentum integral vanishes.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly writes the boundary evaluation and concludes the result is zero.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes the total derivative but does not evaluate the boundary at ±∞.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 0/2; the load-bearing step that makes ⟨p⟩_ψ = 0 for bound states.

items.title: Normalization assumption
items.description: States that the wave function has been assumed normalized.

provenance.discriminates: A response that computes expectation values without acknowledging the normalization assumption.

items.title: Momentum representation integral
items.description: Writes the momentum wave function as χ̃(p) = ∫ dx/(√(2πℏ)) e^{−ipx/ℏ} χ(x).

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference writes this Fourier transform with the factor sqrt and hbar in the final section on the momentum representation.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; explicit requested result, absorption of sign-pitfall item.
